- Users are not the product

- Open in stead of closed

'- When you move instances you can only take your followers with you, not your content.

- No privacy, not encrypted.
- Search function is not good at all

The above are all basic functions. I hope they will be implemented soon.

I also wish we could quote people, as it is very difficult to write about politics as a journalist and activist without that.

Problems of a social nature:

- Most instances are dependent of just one person. If that person fails, gets ill, or turns out to be an asshole, the instance is gone and so is all your content.

- Mastodon is predominantly a white space. People of color don't feel at home because there's a lot of centrism and cocooning. For instance the culture of content warnings is used against people of color, with white users demanding content warnings for racism. The chilling effect is that victims of racism are silenced behind CW walls, while privileged people can have a cosy experience by blocking all toots about racism. This is not how freedom of speech and an open internet should work. 

Although I do understand how CW and the impossibility of quoting is helping to make Mastodon a friendly space, these rules are also protecting privileged people from any criticism. It is clear that Mastodon was written by people that are white, that are also idealistic and rightfully concerned with neurodivergent people, but who fail to realise that their fight against polarisation is preventing change, and protecting the status quo. Not all forms of polarisation are bad; in fact it's very much needed on several levels.

masto_features_hated: Two things: First, there isn't a list of hashtags by use, making it hard to find various communities and by extension users one is interested in. This was intended by design, to make it harder for abuse and harassment to occur, but that has just seen the users who wish to spread abusive messages using a large number of the most visible hashtags in a scattergun approach, so it seems to not stop abuse from needing to be moderated, but it does make it harder to find people. masto_features_loved:
I was lucky to get onto one of the more popular and well-run (both in terms of technical administration and moderation) instances six years ago and the admin has continued to manage it responsibly the whole time.

So I enjoy being able to keep up with friends I had already made as well as find new people to follow and occasionally interact with, with a minimum of friction. Without having existing friends to follow I would have had less motivation to stay on site. My experience and opinion of Mastodon might have been different if I had spent most of my time on a different site.

At the same time, I'm being exposed to people of backgrounds significantly different from mine (I am a cis hetero white male) and I enjoy being able to engage with them and learn from them in a space where they are also comfortable (relative to Twitter et al).
masto_features_hated:
I feel like defederation is sometimes a bigger hammer than is called for. I agree with the necessity of blocking many instances which are overtly racist, antisemetic, anti-queer, etc., frequently under a bad-faith umbrella of using "free speech" motivations to selectively support only their own beliefs.

What I am more ambivalent about are those instances which are not explicitly aligned with repellent interests but get defederated because of individual participants acting in bad faith or who have roles that can be seen as hostile (police, military, journalists). While I don't question a moderator's need to defed a site which itself is not moderated well and consequently is being disruptive to participants on other sites, I worry about the consequences of isolating the people who are not acting in bad faith on those sites and are now cut off from people who would be providing support and helping normalize beliefs that conflict with what the disruptive people say.

masto_features_loved: I really like that Mastodon is open-source and federated, meaning that it cannot be controlled by an individual or a company. Instead, it enables communities to independently manage and moderate themselves. Perhaps the single most valuable feature is Mastodon's interoperabilty with other ActivityPub services, which further ensures the open character of Mastodon.
masto_features_hated:
I find it problematic that almost the entire Mastodon community visible to my home server (meaning except for server-wide blocked neo-nazi instances like Gab or banned individual profiles of Covid conspiracy theorists, Holocaust deniers, Putin supporters etc.) has similar opinions regarding almost all topics.

I've never been to Twitter, but what I hear from its users is constant frustration about ongoing hate-speech and fake-news campaigns by right-wing extremists like the neo-fascist “Alternative für Deutschland” party. Therefore, it is certainly a very good thing that you rarely come across unwanted right-wing profiles. However, it also means a lack of political diversity, since there are hardly any non-left-wing profiles. 

In fact, the only somewhat conservative profile I've seen in my entire 4 years of being a Mastodon user is a member of the German conservative party, but even he has still quite progressive views. You see, especially regarding topics like climate activism, privacy and mass surveillance or workers' strikes, there's hardly any actual discussion, only people agreeing with each other. 

I don't write this because I would disagree with them (in fact, I am one of them regarding many topics), but because I fear that the Mastodon network in its current form is a big echo chamber.

Obviously, this is mainly a problem with the community, but perhaps it's been amplified by the design of Mastodon, which I'm uncertain about though.

FOSS bros who think everyone should use Linux on the desktop 🙃 and are hugely ableist in the process. Also lack of an "followed by [these accounts you also follow]". I'm quite concerned about what might be coming the way of the fediverse in terms of state actors able to run big "bot" operations without more tooling for ordinary users in this regard.
